title: MCP Integration
description: The boot service ships with an MCP server (Streamable HTTP). Other agents can get the endpoint and request body for memory shells and echo/probe shells, then send the HTTP request themselves.
endpoint.title: Endpoint
endpoint.hint: The endpoint follows the current deployment address and keeps any reverse-proxy path prefix; Jar and Docker deployments default to http://127.0.0.1:8080/mcp.
tools.title: Tools
tools.capabilities.description: Lists every supported server, shell tool, shell type, packer, probe method, obfuscation option and obfuscation scope.
tools.memshell.description: Returns a POST request plan (endpoint + body) for a memory shell (Godzilla, Behinder, AntSword, Suo5, Command, etc.); body matches POST /api/memshell/generate. The tool does not generate and never returns the payload.
tools.probe.description: Returns a POST request plan (endpoint + body) for an echo/probe shell (DNSLog, ResponseBody, ResponseHeader, Sleep); body matches POST /api/probe/generate. The tool does not generate and never returns the payload.
clients.title: Connect a client
clients.description: Examples for Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code and Claude Desktop; any other Streamable HTTP client works with the same endpoint.
clients.desktopHint: Claude Desktop only supports stdio, so bridge it through mcp-remote (requires Node.js).
clients.restartHint: Restart the client after saving the configuration.
workflow.title: Workflow
workflow.step1: Call memshell_capabilities first to discover valid server, shellTool, shellType and packer values.
workflow.step2: Call generate_memshell or generate_probe_shell to get endpoint and body.
workflow.step3: Save body to request.json and POST it to endpoint, writing the response to a file, for example curl --data-binary @request.json -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -o memshell.json <endpoint>.
workflow.step4: Read only the fields you need from the JSON with jq, for example jq -r '.memShellResult.shellClassName, .packResult' memshell.json.
workflow.examplePrompt: Call memshell_capabilities first for valid parameters, then call generate_memshell for a Tomcat + Godzilla Filter memory shell, save its body to request.json, POST it to endpoint, and read only the class names and payload from the response file.
security: For authorized security testing and research only.
